newsitem.title: USA: US rate rise hampers budget process - Sen. Harkin.
newsitem.headline: US rate rise hampers budget process - Sen. Harkin.

text.p: Sen. Tom Harkin Tuesday criticized the Federal Reserve's decision to raise interest rates and said it would hamper the budget process.

Harkin, an Iowa Democrat, has been a frequent critic of the Fed and is among a group of lawmakers who believe the central bank should do more to allow the economy to strengthen. He is not a member of the Senate Budget Committee.

"There's no question that the decision by Mr. (Alan) Greenspan and the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates will make it harder for Congress and the President to reach a balanced budget," Harkin said in a statement.

"A rate increase will likely slow economic expansion, thus reducing the amount of revenues coming into the Federal treasury. This Fed muzzle on the economy will only make an already strained budget process even more difficult," he said.
The Fed rate increase brought the federal funds rate that commercial banks charge each other for overnight loans up a quarter of a percentage point to 5.50 percent.
